title.narrative: Diakonia - Governance, active and responsible citizenship 2022-2025
Diakonia - Governance, active and responsible citizenship 2022-2025

description.narrative:
Overall objective: to contribute to the anchoring of democratic culture, the strengthening of democratic institutions and more just, equitable and peaceful governance for the benefit of women and men in Burkina Faso.
The overall objective will be achieved by working towards three specific objectives that each have several expected results:
SO 1: Support reflection and actions to promote a better perception/understanding of democracy and a more just, egalitarian, inclusive and representative democratic practice.
- R1: Public opinion trends in both traditional and social media and especially among young are monitored and analysed in order to develop relevant corrective actions.
- R2: Quality information is produced to fuel reflection, feed and influence public debate, particularly among youth, through ICTs and social media to create an informed public opinion.
- R2: Credible policy information is available and accessible to rights holders to combat misinformation and shape a more balanced opinion on public actions.
- R4: Spaces for interaction are created to put citizens back at the heart of the public debate and give them the tools to act within the democratic system and influence policies and practices.
SO 2: Contribute to implementing innovative and effective initiatives to consolidate civil society's role as a counter-power.
- R1: CSOs can ensure effective governance and management of their organizations.
- R2: The constitutional and institutional reforms adopted are inclusive, structuring and in line with citizens' concerns.
- R3: The capacities of electoral system actors are strengthened to influence elections before, during and after the polls.
- R4: The monitoring system is in place and functional, allowing for real-time monitoring of the electoral process and voting operations, and helping to correct any malfunctions observed on election day and to calm down the voting process.
SO 3: Contribute to creating the conditions for citizens, men, women, youth and usually excluded/marginalized groups to participate in, contribute to and influence different processes at national and local levels.
- R1: Relevant information is produced or made available and accessible to citizens to enable them to understand the issues better and participate effectively in the various processes.
- R2: Women and youth are nominated and elected to decision-making bodies (government, assembly, municipal and regional councils, mayors, governors, prefects, high commissioners, institutions, courts).
- R3: Formal and informal institutional and ad hoc frameworks are available to enable effective and inclusive participation/representation of citizens, including women, youth and traditionally excluded or marginalized groups, in various political and development processes at all levels.
- R4: Land and mineral resources are managed in a participatory manner, revenues from their exploitation are redistributed fairly and invested in priority sectors.

Insatsen syftar till att stärka den demokratiska kulturen, stärka de demokratiska institutionerna och skapa ett mer rättvist, jämlikt och fredligt styrelseskick till förmån för kvinnor och män i Burkina Faso.
I detta syfte kommer insatsen att arbeta för att uppnå tre resultat:
1. Stödja reflektion och aktiviteter för att främja en bättre uppfattning/förståelse av demokrati och en mer rättvis, jämlik, inkluderande och representativ demokratisk praxis.
2. Bidra till genomförandet av innovativa och effektiva initiativ som syftar till att stärka det civila samhällets roll som motkraft.
3. Bidra till att skapa förutsättningar för medborgare, män, kvinnor, ungdomar och traditionellt exkluderade/marginaliserade grupper att delta i, och påverka olika politiska processer och utvecklingsprocesser på nationell och lokal nivå.

The intervention aims to to contribute to the anchoring of democratic culture, the strengthening of democratic institutions and more just, equitable and peaceful governance for the benefit of women and men in Burkina Faso
To this end, the operation will work to achieve three results:
1. Support reflection and actions to promote a better perception/understanding of democracy and a more just, egalitarian, inclusive and representative democratic practice.
2. Contribute to implementing innovative and effective initiatives to consolidate civil society's role as a counter-power.
3. Contribute to creating the conditions for citizens, men, women, youth and usually excluded/ marginalized groups to participate in, contribute to and influence different processes at national and local levels.

The information below springs from reporting, statutory and non-statutory meetings and participation in various activities organized by the cooperation partner.
Diakonia has executed 88 % of the planned activities and 86 % of the budget.
Two difficulties have complicated the work of Diakonia:
These are:
1. The restriction of civic space.
2. A degradation of the security situation.
SO 1: Support reflection and actions to promote a better perception/understanding of democracy and a more just, egalitarian, inclusive and representative democratic practice.
For the purpose of strategic objective 1, Diakonia is collaborating with Association des bloggeurs burkinabé (ABB), Centre pour la Gouvernance Démocratique (CGD - which also receives funding directly from the embassy), Educommunicafrik, Fasocheck and Institut Général Tiémoko Marc GARANGO pour la Gouvernance et le Développement (IGD)
Some key results under this strategic objective includes the setting up of a team of social media monitorers who engaged in continous analysis objective to capture the public opinion online. Fasocheck has engaged in similar monitoring but with a view to analysis desinformation, culminiating each month in a report on desinformation online in Burkina Faso. Educommunicafrique has in turn put into place a Citizen Social Media Observatoire, staffed by 10 "detectives" tasked with monitoring media content shared online and collecting incidents of hate speech (a growing problem in Burkina Faso). Bulletins are then produced on the issue, with a view of feeding into the national discours regarding hate speech.
Diakonia, through its partners, has also worked on creating spaces for educating and informing citizens, particularly young people. For example, CGD organized two training sessions for specific movements (young people from the informal sector, certain members of Wayiyan (a popular social movement made of young men in support of the military junta)) on democratic governance, republican principles and values. IGD also trained 35 young women and men on legislation and issues relating to hate speech and false information. ABB organized two training sessions on democracy and citizen participation. In addition to the training sessions, several other information dialogue forums were organized by the partners. A survey commissioned by Diakonia showed that 91 % of participants felt that their knowledge of governance and democracy had improved thanks to the education provided.
SO 2: Contribute to implementing innovative and effective initiatives to consolidate civil society's role as a counter-power.
Under this strategic objective, Diakonia has worked with the National Council for OSCs (CNOSC) and the Permanent Secretariat of ONGS (SPONG) with the specific am of strengthen the governance and management of civil society organizations in Burkina Faso. Activities include regional conferences on governance of CSOs and workshops on advocacy. In addition, Diakonia has also worked with the National Youth Council (CNJ-BF) in order to strengthen the democratic culture amongst women and youth. Further, through a collaboration with the Convention of civil society organisations for the observation of domestic elections (CODEL) Diakonia supported the development of a new strategic plan, organized 10 meetings for the CODEL, and supported an awareness campaign on electoral questions and democracy aimed at youths, women and journalists in the four biggest cities.
SO 3: Contribute to creating the conditions for citizens, men, women, youth and usually excluded/marginalized groups to participate in, contribute to and influence different processes at national and local levels.
Under this strategic objective Diakonia has supported the Episcopal Commission Justice and Peace (CJP) on the creation of citizen watch cells to monitor local decision-making as well as providing training to these cells with capacity-building measures. Diakonia organized "Citizen Univeristies" for young people, teaching them about civic-mindedness and citizenship, social cohesion, civic participation, gender-based violence, women's and girls' rights and entrepreneurship. In return, 56 of the 60 young people were able to give feedback to their peers on the concepts of social cohesion and gender-based violence, in collaboration with the project team. Of the 60 young people trained, 25 were able to set up income-generating activities and finance their school supplies and school uniforms. They have also set up micro-businesses, and produce article.
